title: His first funeral parade with old man Allen
summary: The first parade he played was a funeral across the river with Red Allen's father, encouraged by his brother-in-law.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: When did you first start playing on the streets? What do you mean on the streets?

Now, the first time I played a parade, I remember, I played with Red Allen's daddy, old man Allen. Played a funeral across the river. Oh, that's been around 1940, oh, 1940 something. It was in the forties, I know. Yeah. I remember somewhere in 1943, 44, or something like that. I mean, I was playing with, uh, I played a parade with him, a funeral with him across the river. And now I'm telling you, man, that was the first time I met an old man Allen, you see? And a man playing that, that funeral man, the first time I ever played a funeral. Because I played the same funeral with my brother-in-law. He's the one that encouraged me to play it, you know? Well, he used to practice, make me practice at home, you know? How did you say, well, you see, you start off on your left feet, and the coordinator would go, da, da, da, da, da, da. I used to, you know, you used to tell me that. So I said, well, I got it. Then I went to the other side. And, matter of fact, I did wonderful on the thing, you know? And from then on, I mean, I started, that was my first funeral. And the first time, matter of fact, I played a parade on the street, you see?
You can't remember who else was in the band?
No, I can't remember who else was in the band. That's been quite a while back there.
